heading: multiview ML-3 — loft silhouette fol-6
text: Read, not measured: a guard run of a tree needs about 1.6 GB (`MR/measure.ts`, MV-3's peaks) and no grant of that size was available to me. What can be said from the code and the tests. (1) `loftRings` is exact for the sections it is given: `🧪️tests/🧊️loft-shape` compares its outlines with the hulls that shapely builds from the same sections (rings of the sections placed by numpy, 29 of 29), so there is no engine defect to repair in how a loft is drawn. (2) The silhouette of an ellipsoid through parallel sections is the hull of its slices and lies inside it by the sag of the step: R(1 - cos(step/2)) of the largest radius, 1.5 % of R at 20 degrees, 0.38 % at 10, 0.1 % at 5, and the same again for the cap beyond the last section; the radii of the 152 ellipsoids of `rowan` at 1:50 are at most 0.9 m, so 14 mm at 20 degrees and 3.5 mm at 10: far from the 42 mm you measure at rest, and the number does not move with `--step`, `--slack` or `--no-fill`. A figure that stays at 42 mm whatever the number of sections is not a sag; it is a place where hulls span something that is not the ellipsoid. (3) In `MV-L1/loft.ts` the beads of the mass hang on one thread (`THREAD`, sections of 0.6 micrometres) and are joined by `walk`: the loft is ONE shape of 284 sections through 12 separate bodies, and `loftRings` hulls every consecutive pair of sections, so every pair of consecutive sections across a gap between two beads is hulled (the engine drops a hull of area below its floor, but a thread section that is not at the right place of the next bead's first ring is not nothing). D54 says what the hand taught: a hand with the thumb beside the palm is one loft per part, never one loft for the hand (31 mm in one, 4 mm in seven). The cure that I can name is the same: one loft per ellipsoid (my tool `🧰️matrix/MX-2/loft.ts` does exactly that for `ellipsoid` solids: nine sections along the longest axis from 10 to 170 degrees, id of the solid; ops entry `{ scale: "50", bone: "fol-6", paint: <the flat outline>, filled: true, replace: [<the flat outline>] }`, `--out` trial, then `MR/measure.ts`), at the price of 12 loft shapes where one stood; the depiction merges shapes of one region. If that measures 15 mm or less at 1:50 the tool of MV-L1 should stop stringing beads; if it does not, send me the trial and the number. (4) An `ellipsoid` drawing solid (an eighth shape geometry) is a schema decision for the dev and I do not take it before a case exists that a loft per ellipsoid cannot draw.
